column2: The repeated in-those-days notices introduce the absence of a king and Dan's search for an inheritance; the selected no-inheritance claim remains despite earlier allotment accounts.
Five strong men from Dan's kindred at Zorah and Eshtaol are sent to inspect and explore; the command and their rest at Micah's house remain.
Recognition concerns the young Levite's voice, followed by three questions about who brought him, his activity and what he has there.
column3: Younger preserves neoteros alongside young man without supplying a comparison group or an explanation of how they knew his voice.

column2: Such and such represents the repeated houtos formula, followed by hiring and becoming Micah's priest; the employment relationship remains.
The request to inquire of God concerns success of their journey; so that gives the contextual connection to their knowing the outcome.
The priest says to go in peace and that their way is before the Lord; he is not made to pronounce an added explicit guarantee of victory.
Confidence is repeated, with the Sidonian pattern, inability to speak a word, distance from Sidon and no dealings with Syria all retained.
column3: Unable to speak a word is opaque in context; no familiar magistrate/oppressor reading is substituted. Syria is the selected geographical name.

column2: The five return to their brothers at both Zorah and Eshtaol; the brothers ask why they sit, not a substituted report-of-results question.
Both arise-and-go-up calls remain, along with the full repeated Laish/Sidon/Syria report, behold, the very good land, the silence question and warning against delay.
column3: Go in compresses go-and-enter in the final movement sequence; no further military success is asserted beyond the speakers' exhortation.

column2: Propose For God has delivered to preserve hoti's explanatory link; the confident people, spacious land and absence of lack remain claims in the scouts' speech.
column3: Your hands renders singular hand with a plural possessor idiomatically; the land/earth sense of ge in the final phrase remains contextually broad.

column2: Six hundred Danites depart from Zorah and Eshtaol equipped for war; the count and both origins remain.
The camp at Kiriath-jearim in Judah explains the continuing Dan's Camp name; look preserves idou and behind preserves the relative location.
They travel onward to Ephraim's hill country and Micah's house, retaining both waypoints.
The five scouts ask about four cult objects in these houses and tell their brothers to consider their action; the plurals and four-item inventory remain.
The young Levite's house is identified with Micah's house; their greeting is not expanded into a request for permission to enter.
The six hundred armed Danites stand firmly at the gateway; their position is retained as the background to the taking.
The five take the carved image, ephod, teraphim and cast image while the priest stands with the armed six hundred; all objects and the two groups remain.
Entry and the four-object taking are repeated before the priest's protest; the apparent repetition is not deleted as redundant.
Silence, hand over mouth and coming with them precede father/priest status and the comparison of one household with a tribe and kindred.
column3: The Greek me question anticipates rejection of the single-house option; the English alternative question preserves the comparison, with that negative rhetorical expectation recorded here.

column2: The priest's glad heart precedes his own taking of the four objects and joining the people's midst; his active participation remains.
The group departs with the whole household and his valuable property in front; the selected singular his remains.
column3: The possessor of his is unclear in the immediate sequence; it is not silently changed to their or expanded to a named owner.

column2: Propose and behold before Micah and his household associates cry after the Danites, restoring the selected idou at the pursuit scene.
The Danites turn their faces and question Micah's cry; what is wrong renders the what-is-to-you idiom naturally.
Micah names the image he made for himself and his priest, asks what remains, and objects to their question; no plural gods is substituted for the selected singular carved image.
The prohibition on his voice leads to a threat from men bitter in soul, with plural you as their target and singular your life in the consequence.
column3: Add your life is unresolved source-visible wording for prostheseis; an implied loss or addition to casualties may be intended, but no missing complement is invented. Lives of your household distributes the collective singular life in English.

column2: The Danites continue while Micah recognizes their superior strength, withdraws and returns home; no renewed pursuit is added.
They carry Micah's objects and priest to quiet, confident Laish, kill by the sword and burn the city; the peaceful description is not recast as military resistance.
No rescue is linked to Sidonian distance and no dealings with people, unlike Syria in verses 7 and 9; Rehob's valley, rebuilding and settlement remain.
Dan names the city after their ancestor born to Israel, replacing its former name Laish; the naming explanation remains.
The image is erected and Jonathan's genealogy explicitly names Gershom and Moses; his descendants' priesthood lasts to the land's deportation.
column3: Moses is the selected reading, not Manasseh; no A/B or Hebrew manuscript collation is claimed and no precise deportation date is supplied.

column2: Micah's image remains established throughout the days of God's house in Shiloh; the parallel duration notice is not collapsed into verse 30.
